framing: full-episode interactional robustness study; NOT a demonstrated IPMA attack
research_question: Holding task goal / identity / facts / decisions / tools / policy / initial DB / official evaluator / max budget fixed, does the user's full-episode interactional expression (urgency / continuation / frustration) change (a) final official task success and (b) tool-use process, and does it depend on model/domain/type?

co_primary_outcomes.P1: official overall reward (binary success), report DB + COMMUNICATE components

multiplicity: Holm over the 4 primary tests (P1/P2 x C3/C4-C1)
inference: task-cluster bootstrap 95% CI + paired label-permutation p; McNemar cross-check for binary reward; mixed-effects models as SENSITIVITY only
itt_rule: ALL frozen episodes analyzed, including no-op / refusal / failure; NO P-responsive eligibility filtering of the primary sample
decision_rules: R1 endpoint effect / R2 endpoint-stable process-sensitive / R3 conditional / R4 calibrated null (state excludable effect) / R5 baseline-infra failure
pre_run_semantic_review: dual-independent-agent (local vLLM); require contamination=0, C3 urgency>C1, C4 frustration>C1, C1 no pressure; fail-closed on disagreement
